rv.q: This production’s power also depends on the musical performance, which threaded beauty and emotional intensity through so much equivocation.
The overall result is a mixed show whose strengths outweigh some perverse idiosyncrasies.
In a Parsifal that is individual all round, nobody is more distinctive than the conductor, Jakub Hrůša.
There's no point at which production and music don't vividly cohere.
Titov's answer is to corrupt the world further and hope the shock passes for insight.
If you don’t, this might just be the one to convert you.
Titov's dreamlike Parsifal manages to infuriate, entertain and provide insight in equal measure.

cn.t: Titov's dystopian staging divides critics with its dark, iconoclastic vision, but Hrůša's superb conducting and the orchestra's radiant playing earn widespread praise in this brutal reimagining of Wagner's final opera.
